value.rationale: Exact sparse atmospheric sensor placement with a necessary unknown ambient level and source amplitude is a motivated estimation problem. The theorem identifies a robust qualitative difference between optimizing all unknowns and the physically central location parameter and quantifies a singular low-background divergence of the array width. Both unique optimizers and their strict separation apply for an entire natural continuum of signal-to-background ratios; this supplies interpretable experimental design guidance rather than an arbitrary tiny numerical improvement. The result is limited to the precise symmetric locally Gaussian Poisson benchmark.
